sources.title: Lerici Foundation: Mrauk U conservation and GIS project (2019)
sources.note: Direct project description read: capital 1430 to 1784, integrated landscape and site-management database. UNESCO nomination work is not inscription on the World Heritage List.

sources.title: Jacques Leider: Tilling the Lord’s Vineyard and Defending Portuguese Interests (2002)
sources.note: Direct full scholarly PDF. Printed39 to 43 political outline and critical reading of Manrique. Do not repeat fanciful numbers or treat Collis historical romance as independent testimony.

sources.title: British Museum: silver tanka of Dharmaraja Hussain, 1882,0508.4
sources.note: Original indexed museum catalogue read; direct open intermittently failed. 1612 to 1622, silver, 29.50mm, 10.05g, Arakanese/Bengali/Persian Arabic inscription scripts. Exact text not exposed; not used as a transcribed writing witness.

sources.title: British Museum: Burma to Myanmar, 1,500 years of connection and isolation
sources.note: Original museum article read: Min Khamaung/Dhammaraja Hussain, Buddhist title with Muslim name and trilingual coin. Hanthawaddy jar is not treated as an Arakan household find.

sources.title: Hans Hägerdal: Slaving, Colonial Diplomacy, and Resource Extraction in Seventeenth-Century Maritime Asia (2024)
sources.note: Original university-repository PDF indexed printed41 verified, including 1643 firman translated from Corpus Diplomaticum I414. Direct retrieval failed; ResearchGate full-text mirror checked same passage. Both mirrors and underlying quoted document pooled.

sources.title: Yan Zhou and colleagues: Shaping cultural landscape from nature, Mrauk-U (2025)
sources.note: Original journal full text indexed and read; section3.2.2 hydraulic system, figures10 and14, methodology. Rainwater as primary supply explicitly an inference; no universal clean-water or sanitation claim. Online2025, volume25(2026) pp5327 to 5346.

sources.title: Marie Gatellier: Le temple Shitthaung à Myohaung (1993)
sources.note: Original Persee indexed page111 verified. Large stone blocks, brick fill, vanished wooden palace and surviving stone enclosure. Earlier chronology and ritual traditions not adopted without separate checking.

sources.title: UNESCO tentative list: Myauk-U archaeological area and monuments, submission824 (1996)
sources.note: Department of Archaeology original submission read. Approximately200 Buddhist monuments, fifteenth/sixteenth-century concentration, vaulting and stone carving. Tentative listing, not inscribed World Heritage status. First-Arakanese-kingdom wording not repeated.

sources.title: Sebastião Manrique: Travels, volume I, translated by C. E. Luard and H. Hosten (1927)
sources.note: Full scholarly translation in 2016 reprint directly read; PDF186 to 187 official washing kit,217 to 218 and226 royal physician/root footnote. dokumen.pub OCR mirror pooled with this work. Confessional agenda and derogatory judgments not adopted. Treatment is narrated belief, not medical efficacy.

sources.title: Thibaut d’Hubert: Patterns of Composition in the Seventeenth-Century Bengali Literature of Arakan (2015)
sources.note: Full original Open Book Publishers chapter mirrored PDF directly read; printed431 gatherings,432 to 434 Ragatala fragments and exact original Roman transliteration/translation,436 to 437 elite teaching. Publisher doi10.11647/OBP.0062.16. Fragments transmitted in later works; no seventeenth-century autograph claimed. All three passages pooled below200 words.

sources.note: Direct original printed125: palace-guard government1692 to 1710, resistance collapsed December1784, capital taken January1785. Distinguish invasion year and final capital capture.

batchIdentityNotes.rationale: Three exact missing indexed phases of the Mrauk U kingdom. The1700 imported princely-state label is erroneous and corrected in proposed overrides. The1650 and1700 polygons are identical; no British-era alias is attached.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Early1492 to 1530 bbox91.4103E,20.4044N,92.8791E,24.0938N omits Mrauk U at93.183E,20.583N. Later1650 to 1783 bbox92.1231E,17.6433N,95.3632E,22.2030N. Exact decoded slices in identities.json. Public caveat retains data error rather than inventing repaired borders.
batchIdentityNotes.excludedReason: Ancient and early-medieval polities differ.1783 to 1878 bridges independent Arakan, Burmese conquest and British rule, requiring a separate narrative.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Public history1430 to January1785; indexed1492 to 1530,1650 to 1700,1700 to 1783 retained. No historical collapse in map gaps. Period1578 approximate start of consolidated Chittagong control.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: No invented universal literacy, household toilets, typical medical effectiveness or original Bengali glyphs. Ordinary work and families appear through water infrastructure, commerce, forced migration and elite teaching; stronger household archaeology not established by these sources.
